procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
GER 21 was represented by Simon Heindl (helm).
SWE 707 was represented by Victor Isdahl (helm).
Mathias Rebholz and Michalina Wroblewska (members of the international jury gave evidence as witnesses.
Max Groy (coasch of GER 21) attended the hearing as an observer.
facts: At the time of the incident the conditions were 5 knots of wind with no waves.
The boats were approaching the downwind finishing line of race 6.
GER 21 was sailing on starboard tack and laying the pin end of the finishing line.
SWE 707 was sailing on port tack, two boat lengths to windward of the port layline towards the pin end of the finishing line.
When entering the zone the boats were overlapped and on a collision course.
When the boats were less than half a boat length apart, SWE 707 bore away and gybed.
When SWE 707 was on starboard tack, GER 21 was overlapped to leeward with less than half a metre distance between the boats.
GER 21 bore away, SWE 707 continued to luff.
Before SWE 707 came to a broad reach the distance between the starboard wing of GER 21 and the port wing of SWE 707 was 10 cm.
SWE 707 luffed, sailed to the pin end of the finishing line, bore away and finished.
No boat took a penalty turn.
conclusions: SWE 707 to windward failed to keep clear of GER 21 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
GER 21 outside overlapped at the zone, gave mark-room to SWE 707 as required by RRS 18.2(a)(1).
Because SWE was not sailing within the mark-room she was entitled to, she is not exonerated for her breach of RRS 11 under RRS 43.1(b).
